s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence
salient_findings: Round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
Lesions range from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
key_facts: Male patient in his 40s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions are round and hypopigmented
Lesions are symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Nevus sebaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic findings of plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis

shortlist.label: Sebaceous nevus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of asymptomatic hypopigmented macules with absence of hair growth and histopathologic findings consistent with sebaceous nevus

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of hypopigmented macules with sharp borders and absence of hair growth, consistent with nevus depigmentosus

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple round hypopigmented macules with varying sizes, consistent with idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis

shortlist.label: Epidermal nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of asymptomatic hypopigmented lesions with histopathologic findings of epidermal changes and neoplastic cords

raw.rationale: The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor are characteristic of Nevus sebaceus.

rejected.label: Sebaceous nevus syndrome
rejected.why: While similar to Nevus sebaceus, Sebaceous nevus syndrome typically involves additional systemic features and more extensive skin lesions, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: Nevus depigmentosus typically presents as a single, well-defined hypopigmented macule, which does not match the multiple, coalescing lesions described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
rejected.why: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis typically presents with multiple, small, discrete hypopigmented macules, but the histopathologic findings do not match those described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Epidermal nevus
rejected.why: Epidermal nevus typically presents with a more linear or streaked appearance, and the histopathologic findings do not match those described in the vignette, which are more characteristic of Nevus sebaceus.
